15.1
INTRODUCTION
Todays world is a world of fashion. The designs of dresses are changing everyday the
world over. India is not farbehind. Indian dress are very popular even in western countries.
One can see fashionable dresses everywhere - at weddings and marriages, in the market,
in fairs, at the university. There is a popular saying which says "wear what others like, eat
what you like" . It is not only the rich and successful who can wear fashionable clothes.
Dress designers today have brought fashion to the masses too. It is easy to design attractive
clothes. One needs to know what is dress designing and the process to be followed in
designing clothes.
15.2
OBJECTIVES
After reading this lesson, you will be able to :
•
explain what is dress designing;
•
demonstrate how to set different designs.
15.3
MEANING
Dress designing refers to shaping the fabric according to the figure and quality of the cloth
by giving an appropriate design.
a)
Meaning of dress.
Dress refers to the garment or set of garments which attractively cover the human

body from top to bottom.
b)
Meaning of designing
.
.
Designing refers to the creation of a new design of a garment without disturbing
thebasic foundationlines.This ineffectmeans mouldingthe basic garmentaccording
to customer's preference and in tune with the prevalent fashion while adding your'
own touch to give it a new look.
Dresses can be made to look attractive by designing. Design can be created to
make dresses out ofless cloth or by combining small pieces of cloth. Designing
makes use of accessories like zari, embroidery, niirrors, metal buttons, lace, sequins
etc to give an attractive look.

consider the climate and the occasion for which the dress is to be used. The design, to
alarge extent, depends upon the use of the garment. The following rules must be kept in
mind while designing:

1.
According to occasion
While designing a dress it is important to consider the occasion for which the dress is to
be worn. Different types of dress are worn while celebrating or mourning.
-
i)
Festive occasion
Bright clothes are preferred on festive occasion like ~~dding or festivals. park
and bright colours reflect the happy mood ofthese occasions. Accessories like

zari, sequins, lace, etc. can successfully be used while designing dresses for such
OCCasIOns.
ii)
Mourning
Dresses in plain designs and light colours are suitable for mourning. They reflect
the sad mood at these times.
2.
Purpose of the dress
While designing a dress we should keep in mind the purpose ofthe dress, i.e. where is
it to be worn, what work will be done when it is worn, etc. Each type of dress has a
different purpose, e.g. a uniform is worn ~ school, formal clothes are worn atwork, party
clothes are worn at a party. etc. Hence, the purpose ofthe dress influences the design.
i)
Party w!!ar
One can select bright, attractive dresses to wear to a party. The dress can be
beautifully designed and in dark colours. One can select dresses fashionably
designedwith lace, embroidery, ribbons etc. One looks attractive wearing a well
designed fashionable dress to party.
.ii)
Club wear
One must be conscious of the fashion of the dress while going to the club but the
dress should also be age appropriate.
iii)
Officer wear
Simple, plain dresses are preferable for office wear. Nevertheless, they must look
good.
iv)·
School wear
A uniform is worn at school. When all the school children wear a uniform, it
establishes a common identity. It also brings all the children at the same level and
prevents inferiority among the children. A uniform is generally made without any
design.
v)
Picnic wear
Dark, rich coloured clothes in good designs are suitable for picnics.
vi)
Work wear
Different types of work requires different types of clothes to be worn. For example,

When dusting or cleaning at home, a duster coat or house coat should be worn;
when cooking an apron should be worn. Mechanics need to wear dungarees
which have many big pockets to hold their tools.
vii)
Night wear
Loose fitting clothes should be worn while sleeping, so that one is comfortable at
night. Hence while designing night wear the two factors to be kept in mind are-
looseness and comfort.
3.
Clothing construction
A design is made on the basis of the body shape. In other words, a design is greatly
influenced by the body shape. For example, one can use frills and smocking to give fullness
to a mess for a thin child. This will help in masking the thinness of the child. If a child is
plump, the dress will have to be designed to make her appear less plum. A dress for a
lady with the following measurements - bust - 36", waist 25", hip - 40", will have to be
so designed that it looks decent on the body.

Style emphasis
The basicpointtobe kept inmind while designing isthat thedesign shouldemphasise
the good features of the wearer and conceal any figure defects. For example, if

Treatment of major points
One must prepare a sketch to see what the final design is going to look like and
the body structure of the wearer has to be kept in mind while designing. For
example, a dress for a person with a thin, long neck can be designed to have a
collar or a neck band.
Hi)
Prominent style point
Every dress has one prominent stylepoint which governs other things. For example,
in a gents shirt, the collar is the most prominent feature. A shirt can be made very

15.5 CONCEPT
OF DRESS DESIGNING
The following factors should be considered while designing a dress:
i)
Styie
The style in which a dress is to be made has to consider many things like the
texture and weave of the fabric, the colour, fall, etc. If these things are not kept
in mind while setting the design the final product will not look attractive.
ii)
Weave
The weave and texture of the fabric influence the design to a great degree. A dress
, of light material to be worn in summers will be loose and open whereas a Oress
to be worn in winter will have collar, full selves, etc. Features like smocking or
honey combing can not be used on heavy fabrics but tucks, pleats, etc. can easily
be used.
iii)
Weather
Clothes should ideally be designed according to the weather. Clothes meant to be
worn in winters can be made of heavy, thick fabrics. They can have full sleeves,
close fitting, heavy designs, frills, etc. Whereas clothes to be worn in summer
should be made of light fabrics, with simple designs and in light colours.
iv)
Colour
The colour of clothes Shouldcomplement the figure and complexion of the wearer.
This is an important feature to consider otherwise even the best designed dress
will not look attractive on the wearer.

v)
Trimming material
The trimming material should be used according to the design and it should be -
used in correct proportions. Too much or too little trimming material will make the
dress appear unattractive. Trimming material could be-
,-
a)
tailor made trimming material
b)
decorative trimming material
vi)
Design
The design on a dress should not be too heavy or too light. In both cases, the
dress will not be very attractive. Hence, a proportionate amount of design should
be used on a dress.
Advantages
1)
Fitting
If the above factors are kept in mind while designing a dress, the final product is
-sure to have a good fitting and will look attractive.
2)
Fashion
A dress according to the latest fashion c,aneasily be designed while keeping the
factors such as weather, style, figure, etc. in mind.
3)
Attractive
A well designed dress will look attractive and be much in demand. It is rightly
said-
"Godmade man
And the tailor makes him attractive".
Dress can be made attractive by designing and can effectively improve the
-personality of an individual.
